text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Economic growth is expected to slow to 5.7 percent this year, compared to 6.1 percent last year, mainly due to stagnation in the industrial sector at around 4.0 percent.
- The government plans to merge the Investment Corp of Pakistan and National Investment Trust ahead of their eventual privatisation.
- Small engineering units are subject to 19 different taxes and control by 30 different government departments each exacting its own undocumented taxation, according to a study by a group of experts.

- The caretaker government has decided to abandon the accountability process after the chief accountability commissioner sent back more than half the cases because they lacked sufficient evidence or contained procedural flaws.
- The Punjab government continued a crackdown against sectarian parties and rounded up more activists belonging to Tehrik-i-Jafria, Sipah-i-Sahaba and Sipah-i-Mohammad.
- Interior Minister Umer Khan Afridi has ruled out any disqualification of contesting candidates or the leaders of any political party before the February 3 polls.
- Pakistan Telecommunication Co Ltd will increase line rent and connection charges by almost 100 percent in the next few days.
- The joint venture partners in the proposed Iran-Pak Oil Refinery plan to offer a guaranteed dividend of not less than 60 percent of the net profits to attract public subscription .
- Nearly a dozen people were reportedly drowned in a boat mishap in River Ravi in central Pakistan.
